newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end firm, blue chips up.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end firm, blue chips up.

text.p: Singapore shares ended higher on Thursday with selective blue chips firmer, dealers said.
"The market is quiet except for a technical rebound in selective blue chips and some small cap stocks," said an institutional dealer.
Favourite index blue chips Cerebos, Cycle & Carriage, Fraser & Neave and Keppel Corp rose between 30 and 20 cents, pushing the key Straits Times Industrials Index up 15.86 points to 2,110.34.
Market volume was thin 83.48 million shares with advances ahead of declines by 178 to 124.

Foreign tranches of blue chips made a strong comeback with Singapore Press foreign leading the top gainers, up Singapore 90 cents (US$0.64) to S$23.90 on a volume of 392,000 shares. SIA foreign also remained firm, gaining 30 cents to S$14.50.

System integrator and telecommunication company Teledata led volume with 6.40 million shares changing hands. The share was up S$0.015 at S$0.92 and saw a block deal of 6.0 million shares done at S$0.90.
Malaysia's IJM Corp and Metallock were among losers, easing 26 and 13 cents respectively.
